Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Patel, COO; and Lisa Wong, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Thompson, CEO of ShopNova.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by evolving customer purchasing habits that boosted order frequency and positive trends in average order value, alongside exciting early traction from our new product launches. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV and active customers.

Our focus remains on preparing robustly for the holiday season with optimized inventory levels and demand forecasting. We are also investing heavily in AI-driven personalization and logistics enhancements.

Finally, we are committed to delivering on our profitability outlook while expanding our marketplace ecosystem.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jamie. Our Q3 revenue was $3.42 billion, an increase of 16% year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.2%, driven by improved supply chain efficiencies and a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin categories. Operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 61% of revenue. Our marketing investments remained disciplined, scaling efficiently with ROI-focused campaigns on social commerce platforms.

Our net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance, which I'll detail shortly.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO of ShopNova, your leading omnichannel e-commerce platform serving over 150 million active customers globally, today I'd like to dive deep into one of our core customer engagement KPIs: order frequency, which we define as the average number of orders placed per active customer over the trailing 12 months. This metric is a leading indicator of customer stickiness, directly influencing customer lifetime value—or LTV—which we've historically modeled at a 3.2x multiplier on annual customer value for our top cohorts.

In Q3 FY2024, we delivered a robust 14% year-over-year increase in order frequency, rising from 4.2 orders per customer to 4.8. This marks our strongest quarterly performance in two years and outpaces the broader e-commerce industry benchmark of 8-10% growth, as reported by recent McKinsey Digital Commerce surveys. For context, this improvement contributed approximately 220 basis points to our overall revenue per user growth, helping offset softer average order values in commoditized categories like apparel amid inflationary pressures.

Let me break this down by key drivers and segments. First, repeat customer cohorts—those with at least two orders in the prior year—saw the most pronounced uplift, with order frequency jumping 18% YoY to 6.1 orders per customer. This was fueled by our AI-driven personalization engine, OmniAI 2.0—now rebranded as NovaAI—which leverages collaborative filtering and real-time behavioral data to deliver hyper-targeted recommendations. For instance, in beauty and personal care, where we compete head-to-head with Sephora and Ulta Beauty's digital arms, cross-sell prompts increased add-to-cart frequency by 22%, turning a single lipstick purchase into bundled regimens 35% more often.

New customer acquisition, while still ramping, showed early promise with a 9% YoY lift to 1.9 orders per customer in their first 90 days post-signup. Here, our 'QuickReplenish' subscription model—similar to Amazon Subscribe & Save but with dynamic pricing tied to inventory velocity—played a pivotal role. Penetration reached 28% of new grocery orders, up from 19% last year, driving habitual monthly replenishments for staples like household essentials and meal kits. This initiative has reduced churn in the high-velocity grocery vertical by 15%, aligning us closer to Instacart's 2.2x frequency benchmarks.

Regionally, the trends vary meaningfully, reflecting localized habits and macroeconomic tailwinds. In North America, which accounts for 52% of our GMV, order frequency hit 5.6—our highest ever—bolstered by Walmart+ and Target Circle integrations that mimic Amazon Prime's free shipping threshold. U.S. customers are ordering 25% more frequently in health & wellness, spurred by post-pandemic self-care trends and our partnerships with brands like Peloton for bundled fitness gear.

APAC, representing 28% of GMV, grew 12% YoY to 4.2 orders per customer, led by Southeast Asia where mobile-first habits dominate. In Indonesia and India, akin to Shopee and Flipkart markets, we saw a 30% surge in fashion micro-orders via our TikTok Shop API feeds, with Gen Z cohorts averaging 7.5 orders annually—driven by live-streaming flash sales that compress purchase cycles to under 24 hours.

EMEA lagged slightly at 11% YoY growth to 3.9 orders, pressured by regulatory hurdles like the EU's DMA and softer consumer sentiment in the UK post-Brexit. However, our localized initiatives, such as Zalando-inspired wardrobe subscriptions in Germany and France, boosted fashion frequency by 19%, mitigating headwinds from higher logistics costs.

Technically, these gains stem from several strategic pillars. We've invested $150 million in FY2024 CapEx for RFM segmentation enhancements—recency, frequency, monetary analysis—at the cohort level, powered by Snowflake and our proprietary ML models on AWS Bedrock. This has improved next-best-action accuracy by 40%, prioritizing upsell bundles in checkout flows. Additionally, our iOS and Android app push notification engine, with 65% open rates, now incorporates geofencing for 'near-me' deals, lifting impulse frequency by 16% in urban markets.

Looking ahead, we expect order frequency to accelerate to 5.2 by fiscal year-end, supported by three initiatives: (1) launching 'NovaClub Pro' loyalty tiers with 5% cashback on high-frequency categories, targeting a 20% uptake among our 40 million Prime-eligible users; (2) expanding QuickReplenish to apparel via AI-predicted style refreshes, akin to Stitch Fix's model; and (3) piloting drone delivery in select U.S. metros to shave fulfillment times below 2 hours, which our internal pilots show boosts frequency by 12-15% through habit formation.

In summary, these shifts in purchasing habits underscore a broader industry transition toward 'commerce as a service'—from transactional to relational. We're not just selling products; we're embedding into daily routines, much like how Alibaba's Taocaicai has transformed neighborhood grocery in China. This positions ShopNova for sustained LTV expansion, even as we navigate competitive intensity from Temu and Shein.

Next, I'd like to turn to average order value, or AOV, trends and the key factors driving changes. As you know, AOV—calculated as total revenue divided by total orders—is a critical KPI in e-commerce, directly influencing gross merchandise value (GMV) efficiency and customer lifetime value (CLV) without proportionally scaling acquisition costs.

In Q3 2024, our global AOV came in at $48.72, marking a robust 8.2% year-over-year increase from $45.01, and a sequential 2.1% uptick from Q2. This performance exceeded our internal guidance of 5-7% YoY growth and contributed approximately 320 basis points to our overall revenue expansion. For context, this outpaces the broader e-commerce industry average, where Shopify's merchant cohort reported a modest 2-4% AOV growth amid softening consumer spend.

Let me break down the key drivers, categorized by strategic initiatives, product mix shifts, regional dynamics, and macroeconomic tailwinds/headwinds.

First, personalization and recommendation engine enhancements were the primary upside driver, with a +4.8% AOV impact. Our AI-powered recommendation engine, built on a TensorFlow-backed collaborative filtering model similar to Amazon's 'Frequently Bought Together' features, appeared in 68% of checkout funnels, driving a 12% conversion lift on add-to-cart items. For instance, bundling complementary products—like pairing Nike Air Max sneakers with Under Armour apparel—boosted basket size by an average of 1.7 items per order.

We rolled out 'Dynamic AOV Optimizers' leveraging real-time customer segmentation via our proprietary NovaML platform. This targeted high-intent users with tailored bundles, resulting in a 15% AOV uplift in that cohort. Early A/B test data shows a 22% add-to-basket rate for electronics bundles.

Second, loyalty and subscription program expansion added +2.3% to AOV. ShopNova Prime now boasts 28 million members, up 22% YoY, delivering 35% higher AOV at $65.41 versus $38.92 for non-members. 'Prime Perks' threshold incentives reduced cart abandonment by 18%.

Third, product mix shifts contributed +3.1%. Electronics AOV jumped 14% to $112.34, home & garden rose 9% to $72.18, while fashion dipped slightly but was offset by premium private-label lines.

Regionally, North America hit $52.14 (+10.5% YoY), EMEA $44.29 (+4.2%), APAC $51.87 (+12.1%), and LATAM held flat.

Macro headwinds like interest rates created a -1.9% net drag, but we optimized via dynamic pricing.

Looking ahead, we're targeting 7-9% AOV growth through GenAI chat commerce, AR try-on, and B2B expansion.

Now, on new product and service launches, which drove 28% YoY GMV growth to $27.2 billion this quarter. We've executed on NovaFresh same-day delivery, StyleAI virtual wardrobe personalization, and NovaEssentials private-label grocery line.

NovaFresh, rolled out in 12 U.S. metros, accounted for 18% of orders, $320 million GMV, 22% repeat lift, 14% AOV increase to $128. NPS 72, with strong feedback on speed.

StyleAI boosted apparel conversions 32%, AOV to $95, $450 million GMV. NPS 68, high satisfaction on fits.

NovaEssentials captured 8% grocery GMV ($280 million), 42% margins. NPS 65, low churn.

These build our data moat for 2.5x LTV uplift.

Turning to holiday season preparations, which drive 35-40% of annual GMV. Our AI forecasting projects $4.2-4.5 billion holiday GMV, 22-28% growth. Electronics +38%, apparel +18%, home +25%, beauty +20%.

U.S. 26% growth (62% mix), Europe 30%, APAC 35%.

Inventory at $1.8 billion peak, 8.2x turns. Forecast accuracy 92% via Snowflake and Blue Yonder. Expanded DCs, diversified sourcing.

Finally, our forward guidance for Q4 FY2024 and full FY2025. Q4 GMV $28.5-29.5 billion (19-24% YoY), full-year $118-122 billion (18-22%). Revenue Q4 $3.55-3.65 billion (14-18%), full-year $14.8-15.3 billion (15-19%). Adjusted EBITDA Q4 $650-700 million (18.3-19.2% margin), full-year $2.85-3.0 billion (19.2-19.6%).

Drivers: marketplace growth, regional momentum, category strength. Margin expansion from gross margin to 28.5-29.0%, OpEx leverage. CapEx 4.5-5% of revenue, FCF $2.4 billion.

Risks: tariffs, FX, consumer confidence. Upside: social commerce, B2B.

Now I'll turn it over to Mike to discuss operations.

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment scalability. Our shipping times improved by 25% year-over-year. Fulfillment costs declined 18% as a percentage of GMV. We are implementing advanced robotics in 20 warehouses, boosting throughput by 40%.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Mike. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our TikTok influencer partnerships and Prime Day extensions. Customer acquisition costs were flat at $22. Our brand awareness increased by 15% per Nielsen data. We are focusing on hyper-personalized social commerce and loyalty program expansions.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for participating in the question and answer session will be given momentarily. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs.

David Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, can you expand on the sustainability of the 14% order frequency growth, especially in EMEA where it lagged? Any specific initiatives there?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, David. Great question. In EMEA, while growth was 11% to 3.9, our Zalando-inspired subscriptions boosted fashion by 19%. We're accelerating with localized wardrobe models and geofenced notifications, expecting catch-up to global averages by year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Carter:
Hi team, on forward guidance, how are you factoring in potential U.S. tariffs? And what's the sensitivity?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, we've baked in conservative 1-2% GMV headwind from 10-20% tariffs. Sensitivity: every 5% tariff hike shaves 0.5% off GMV, but our diversified sourcing—40% Vietnam/India—mitigates. Upside from NovaFresh scaling offsets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
Strong AOV lift—impressive. Mike, how did personalization ops tie into that? Any fulfillment impacts?

Mike Patel:
Raj, thanks. Our NovaAI integrations directly supported bundling, with robotics handling the larger baskets seamlessly. No added strain; in fact, denser orders improved efficiency by 12%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Kim with Barclays.

Sophia Kim:
Lisa, early feedback on StyleAI is great—how's marketing amplifying new launches like NovaEssentials?

Lisa Wong:
Sophia, we're running targeted TikTok campaigns with 8:1 ROAS, tying into influencer unboxings. Grocery subscriptions via app pushes have 62% uptake on 'value' messaging, aligning with NPS trends.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie Thompson for closing remarks.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
